title: California's 50th Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for California's 50th Congressional District features seven-term Democratic incumbent Scott Peters facing Republican challenger Steve Cohen, a former KUSI-TV news director. The district covers coastal and inland San Diego County communities including La Jolla, Point Loma, Coronado, downtown San Diego, Poway, and parts of San Marcos and Escondido. Registered Democrats outnumber Republicans in the district by nearly a 2-to-1 margin. Cook Political Report rated the race as 'Solidly Democratic' ahead of the June 2 primary.
polling_note: No independent public opinion polls were found specifically for the CA-50 general election matchup as of June 2026. Cook Political Report rated the race 'Solid Democratic' before the primary.

candidates.name: Scott Peters
candidates.summary: Incumbent Congressman Scott Peters is seeking a seventh full term representing California's 50th District. First elected in 2012, he previously served on the San Diego City Council (becoming the first City Council President) and as chairman of the San Diego Unified Port District. In Congress, he serves on the House Energy and Commerce and Budget Committees and is known for bipartisan work on environmental policy, veterans issues, and fiscal responsibility.

candidates.name: Steve Cohen
candidates.summary: Steve Cohen is a former KUSI-TV news director and Republican candidate challenging incumbent Scott Peters. With 50 years in television news, including 20 years as KUSI's news director, Cohen retired from broadcasting in 2023 and was recruited by the San Diego County Republican Party to run. His campaign emphasizes border security, fiscal accountability, protecting Social Security and Medicare, and making San Diego affordable for working families.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific public general-election polling was found, so this forecast rests entirely on non-polling fundamentals. Scott Peters is a seven-term Democratic incumbent in a district where registered Democrats outnumber Republicans by nearly 2-to-1. Cook Political Report rated the race 'Solid Democratic' before the June 2 primary. The Republican challenger, Steve Cohen, is a former TV news director and first-time candidate with no elected office experience. These factors combine to indicate an overwhelming Democratic advantage. Confidence remains medium rather than high due to the complete absence of published general-election matchup polls, which introduces more uncertainty than a polled race would carry.
